title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Construction of News: Challenges and Opportunities Facing Journalism in an Age Underlined by Increasing Distrust in Knowledge-Producing Institutions

detail.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Construction of News: Challenges and Opportunities Facing Journalism in an Age Underlined by Increasing Distrust in Knowledge-Producing Institutions
detail.abstract: News is constructed through a myriad of processes reflecting the cultural and social context in which newsrooms operate as well as the work routines and ownerships structures that govern news organisations. Natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning algorithms have now enabled news organisations to automate content creation, significantly improving efficiency. These algorithms can analyse data, generate headlines, and write news articles. Such innovations have opened opportunities for journalists to focus on investigative journalism and in-depth reporting, while also providing real-time news to an information-hungry audience. However, the rise of AI in news construction also brings its own set of challenges, one of the most significant issues being trust. This paper discusses how AI is used in news organisations, highlighting successful projects and lessons learned. The democratisation of content creation and the potential for personalised, data-driven news experiences also hold immense promise. This paper notes that the industry must grapple with profound issues of trust, ethics, and transparency to maintain the integrity of journalism in an era where traditional knowledgeproducing institutions are met with scepticism.

title: Does Green Trust Mediate the Relationship between Green Knowledge and Purchasing Behaviour of the Youth in Saudi Arabia?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Does Green Trust Mediate the Relationship between Green Knowledge and Purchasing Behaviour of the Youth in Saudi Arabia?
detail.abstract: This study investigates how consumer purchasing behaviour is impacted by green knowledge and green trust. In addition, it examines the way green trust mediates the relationship between green knowledge and purchasing behaviour. As environmental concerns are more widely discussed, understanding what the factors are influencing green purchase decisions is crucial. By using convenience sampling, distributing surveys to Saudi Arabian consumers who had different backgrounds helped in data collection. The rresearchers used structural equation modelling to study the data. The results show that green trust influences green purchasing behaviour positively and mediates the relationship between green knowledge and green purchasing behaviour partially. The results confirm the direct effect of green knowledge on green trust and green purchasing behaviour was positive. Likewise, green trust is correlated with better green knowledge, which improves the chances of consumers indulging in green purchase behaviour. The study also attempts to determine how the relationships between the variables may affect marketers and representatives interested in greener consumption. By promoting green expertise, companies can build credibility.

title: What Moves the Price of Gold: An Economic-Scarcity Lens on Policy, the Dollar, and the Debasement Trade

detail.title: What Moves the Price of Gold: An Economic-Scarcity Lens on Policy, the Dollar, and the Debasement Trade

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants, patients, or case studies requiring ethics approval. All data used are publicly available.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted independently, without external funding or institutional support.

detail.abstract: What moves the price of gold? I answer this with an economic scarcity lens that equates value with the product of (i) desirability, transmitted mainly by real interest rates and the U.S. dollar and expressed through ETFs, futures, and official purchases, (ii) physical scarcity, captured by gold's high stock to flow and slow supply response, and (iii) an interaction that scales price sensitivity in tight markets. The contribution is both general and particular. In general, the paper organizes all drivers into this mechanism first structure, derives a policy transmission map from hikes and cuts, QE and QT, and repression to gold via real rates, term and liquidity premia, and the dollar, and states a minimal algebra of signs with a practical indicator dashboard. In particular, the same lens is used to interpret the 2024 to 2025 "debasement trade": why expected real rate compression and reserve diversification can lift gold even when contemporaneous real yields are firm, and what observable developments would falsify the narrative (rising real rates, a persistently stronger dollar, or flow reversals). The framework clarifies when gold is likely to hedge effectively and when it is not.

title: Monetary Policy Effectiveness in a Multi-Sector Model: The Amplifying Role of Hand-to-Mouth Households
affiliations: Florida International University (FIU) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Monetary Policy Effectiveness in a Multi-Sector Model: The Amplifying Role of Hand-to-Mouth Households
detail.abstract: This paper quantitatively investigates how the effectiveness of monetary policy varies with the share of hand-to-mouth (HtM) households across countries. We calibrate a multi-sector Two-Agent New Keynesian (TANK) model for a diverse sample of 65 economies, using country-specific empirical estimates for HtM household shares and detailed input-output data to discipline each country's production structure. Our central finding is that HtM households act as a powerful amplifier of the monetary transmission mechanism. A contractionary monetary policy shock induces a substantially larger and more rapid decline in aggregate consumption and real output in economies with a higher prevalence of HtM households. We find that the amplification effect is economically large, with the consumption response in high-HtM countries being an order of magnitude stronger than in low-HtM countries. This heterogeneity has profound implications, showing that the potency of monetary policy is not a universal constant but varies predictably with the financial structure of the household sector. Our results highlight the need for central banks, particularly in emerging markets, to calibrate policy with careful consideration of local household financial conditions.

title: Brexit and its Impact on EU Financial Markets
affiliations: Lancaster University Management School, University of Illinois Springfield,  and University of Westminster

detail.title: Brexit and its Impact on EU Financial Markets
detail.abstract: We investigate the impact of Brexit on volatility spillovers across the EU countries. We introduce a Brexit intensity measure that assigns an intensity score reflective of the financial markets' reaction to the events that occurred as Brexit negotiations began to unfold. We find that Brexit related events have contributed towards increased volatility transmission within the EU. Countrywise investigations show that throughout the Brexit timespan, France is the key volatility transmitter within the Union. By contrast, the UK is evidenced as a volatility transmitter during the early stages of Brexit negotiations, under Theresa May as the prime minister. Out of the smallest stock markets of the block, Ireland, Portugal, and Spain have been amongst those particularly affected.

title: Analysts' Capital Expenditure Forecasts and Bank Debt Contracting
affiliations: , University of Southampton and University of Piraeus, Department of Banking and Financial Management

detail.title: Analysts' Capital Expenditure Forecasts and Bank Debt Contracting
detail.abstract: This study investigates the role of financial analysts' capital expenditure (capex) forecasts in shaping bank loan contracting terms, particularly loan pricing. While prior research has largely focused on earnings forecasts and equity market outcomes, we explore how capex forecasts, an increasingly prevalent and informative signal, are associated with lenders' debt financing. We argue that analyst capex forecasts provide lenders with credible, external assessments of firms' growth opportunities and investment plans, thereby reducing information asymmetry and agency concerns. Using a comprehensive sample of U.S. bank loans, we find that a greater number of analyst capex forecasts is significantly associated with lower loan spreads. This effect is more pronounced when forecasts are issued by analysts with greater firm-specific experience, industry expertise, or a strong track record of forecast accuracy. We also find that the association is stronger for borrowers with higher information asymmetry and weaker when lenders are more sophisticated and experienced. Furthermore, analyst capex forecasts are linked to more favorable non-price loan terms, including a lower likelihood of collateral requirements and capex-related covenant restrictions. Our findings extend the growing literature on the informational role of analysts in debt markets and highlights the broader economic relevance of non-earnings forecasts.
